stem: Which state had the highest constructed road length under Bháratmala Pariyojana as of 31st October 2024?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Up to 31 October 2024, under the Bharatmala Project, the highest length of constructed roads was in Rajasthan (2,241 km), which was more than Uttar Pradesh (1,854 km) and Maharashtra (1,837 km). By October 2025, a total of 21,351 km of roads had been constructed under the Bharatmala Project. In terms of total constructed length, the top three states were Rajasthan (2,258 km), Uttar Pradesh (2,084 km), and Maharashtra (1,960 km).

stem: The Bharatmala Project is related to which infrastructure sector of India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: The Bharatmala Project is related to India’s road infrastructure. It is a national programme for the construction and upgradation of national highways. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I in October 2017. Its duration was five years, from 2017–18 to 2021–22. Phase-II of the Bharatmala Project was announced in January 2021.

stem: How many national Highways are there in India and approximately what is their total length?
expl: In the context of the question period, option (d) was the correct answer. As of 31 December 2024, the total length of national highways in India was approximately 146,195 km.

stem: What is the Golden Quadrilateral?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Under the first phase of the National Highways Development Project, the Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai. Its total length is 5,846 km. The North–South Corridor connects Srinagar with Kanyakumari, while the East–West Corridor connects Silchar with Porbandar.

stem: Which of the following two extreme locations are connected by the East-West Corridor?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The East–West Corridor connects Silchar in Assam with Porbandar in Gujarat. The North–South Corridor connects Srinagar with Kanyakumari. Both corridors were constructed under the National Highways Development Project.

stem: ........ carries 40 percent of road traffic of India –
expl: As of 31 March 2019, the total length of national highways was 1,32,499 km, which constituted only 2.09 percent of the total road length of the country. However, nearly 40 percent of the total road traffic of India is carried through national highways. According to the Annual Report 2024-25 of the Ministry of Road, Transport and Highways, the total length of national highways in India is 146,195 km.

stem: The railways in India was first opened in –
expl: During the period of Lord Dalhousie, the first railway route in India was completed in 1853. On 16 April 1853, the first train was run between Mumbai (then Bombay) and Thane.

stem: The width between two rails of Broad gauge is –
expl: On the basis of gauge (distance between two rails), railways are classified into three categories— (1) Metre gauge—distance between the two rails is 1 metre. (2) Broad (or broad line)—distance between the two rails is 1.676 m or 1676 mm or 5½ feet. (3) narrow gauge—distance between the two rails is 762 mm or 610 mm.

stem: The Railway Zone Headquarter Hajipur is located in –
expl: At present, Indian Railways is divided into 17 zones (with headquarters). Among these, the East Central Railway has its headquarters at Hajipur in Bihar. The Hajipur headquarters began functioning from 1 October 2002. In February 2019, the formation of the 18th zone—South Coast Railway (Visakhapatnam)—was announced.

stem: Which one of the following numbered Rajdhani trains covers the longest distance?
expl: The Thiruvananthapuram Central Rajdhani Express (Train No. 12431) covers the maximum distance. It covers about 3149 km between Thiruvananthapuram Central and Hazrat Nizamuddin. In comparison, Dibrugarh Town covers 2459 km, Bengaluru Rajdhani covers 2365 km, and Chennai Central covers 2175 km.

stem: Konkan Railway passes through which states?
expl: Konkan Railway passes through Maharashtra–Goa– Karnataka. It starts from Roha station (Maharashtra), passes through Madgaon (Goa), and ends at Mangaluru station (Karnataka). Its total length is about 741 km.

stem: ‘Rupsi Airport’ is located in which state of India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Rupsi Airport is located in Kokrajhar district of Assam. It is operated by the Airports Authority of India (AAI).

stem: Paradip is located in the state of –
expl: Paradip Port was developed mainly for the export of iron ore near the Odisha coast. Various goods, including iron ore, are imported and exported from here.

stem: Marmugao seaport is situated in –
expl: Mormugao Port is located in the state of Goa, at the mouth of the Zuari River.

stem: India’s 13th major port is going to be set up in which state?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: India’s 13th major port is going to be established in the state of Maharashtra. The Union Cabinet took this decision on 5 February 2020. The port will be developed at Vadhavan near Dahanu in Maharashtra.

stem: national Waterway-1 connects -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly river waterway is National Waterway No. 1. It extends from Prayagraj (Allahabad) to Haldia.

stem: Jawaharlal nehru Port is located in the State of:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority: JNPA) is located in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra. It is India’s major container-handling port. At present, JNPA operates five container terminals—Nhava Sheva Freeport Terminal, Nhava Sheva International Container Terminal, APM Terminal, Gateway Terminals India, and Bharat Mumbai Container Terminal.

stem: Which of the following ports is an artificial port?
expl: Among the given Indian ports, Chennai is an artificial port. Its commercial operations began in 1881. It is the third oldest major port in India. Mormugao, Mumbai, and Kochi are natural ports.

stem: The renamed name of Kandla Port is—

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Kandla Port is located in Kachchh district of Gujarat. It is one of India’s major ports and has been renamed as Deendayal Port. It is a tidal port. The Kandla Free Trade Zone was India’s first free trade zone.

stem:
Arrange the following ports of India from north to south:
1. Kakinada 2. Machilipatnam
3. nagapattinam 4. visakhapatnam
Choose the correct answer using the code given below:

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The correct north-to-south arrangement of the ports is: Visakhapatnam – Kakinada – Machilipatnam – Nagapattinam.

stem: The Pass, which is situated at the highest elevation, is

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Among the given options, Nathu La is situated at the highest altitude. The altitude of Nathu La is 14,140 feet (4,310 meters). Zoji La is at 11,650 feet (3528 meters), Rohtang Pass at 13,051 feet (3,978 meters), and Khyber Pass at 3,510 feet (107 Meters). However, the highest pass in India is Yangzi Diwan (5890 meters). Since none of the above is mentioned in the options, the correct answer to this question is option (e).

stem: When was ‘Speed Post Service’ launched by the Indian Postal department in competition to the ‘Courier service’?
expl: The ‘Speed Post’ service was started by the Indian Postal Department on 1 August 1986.

stem: Topographical map of India is prepared by which organization?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Topographical maps of India are prepared by the Survey of India. It works under the Department of Science and Technology. The headquarters of the Survey of India is in Dehradun, Uttarakhand.

stem: In which of the following countries is the city of Hyderabad located?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Hyderabad is the capital of Telangana state. There is also a Hyderabad in Pakistan. Therefore, since more than one option is correct, the correct answer will be option (e).

stem: The Black Revolution is related to the

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Black Revolution is related to the production of petroleum (crude oil). Other major revolutions and their production are as follows— Blue Revolution: fish production; Green Revolution: foodgrain production; Red Revolution: meat and tomato production; Yellow Revolution: oilseed production; Pink Revolution: onion/meat/poultry/shrimp production.

stem: The Grey Revolution is related to which of the following?
expl: The Grey Revolution is related to fertilizer production, whereas the Blue Revolution is related to fisheries, the Yellow Revolution to oilseed production, and the Gol (Round) Revolution to potato production.

stem: Which place is called the Silicon valley of India?
expl: Bangalore (Bengaluru) in Karnataka is known as the Silicon Valley of India.

stem: Which of the following is a technopolis?
expl: Among the given options, Silicon Valley is an example of a technopolis. High-technology industries that are regionally concentrated, self-reliant and highly specialized are called a technopolis (technology hub). Silicon Valley near San Francisco, Silicon Forest near Seattle, and Silicon Valley in India are major examples of a technopolis.
